title: RAW UNREVIEWED: transparent heaven, opaque body, and light form one causal reading chain
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Use the already reviewed medieval source distinction between transparent heaven, an opaque celestial body, and light/illumination to propose one connected three-role construction: the heaven is a transmitting location or medium, the body is an actor or occluder within it, and light is the resulting mobile or blocked effect. Whole target unit proposed for later author review is the complete admitted f89v1.13–20 text, with every group and line retained. Assign no Voynich words now. The reading would change if any full clause treats a body as the transmitter or uses light as an entity located in heaven rather than as an effect. Rival: an astronomical catalogue places three independent labels together without a causal chain. Existing IDEA781 tests opposite received/sent light roles; this proposal concerns mediation through a distinct transparent medium and body role. Target role binding and lexical values remain unknown; no new target access or significance is claimed.

design.mechanism: A single whole clause composes transparent heaven as medium, opaque body as participant or blocker, and light as a directed result; participant attachment must stay stable through any following clause.
design.unit: The complete already-owned target text f89v1.13–20, with all groups and line boundaries, considered against the already read complete Morgan M.652 f5r/f5v source account.
design.contrast: A causal medium-body-effect construction versus an unordered sky catalogue, one generic Sun/Moon label, or IDEA781-style sender/receiver polarity alone.
design.prediction: A future complete author reading must assign noninterchangeable roles to heaven, body, and light and explain each written attachment across the full unit; if only one or two role classes can be assigned, or one body/light referent must swap arbitrarily, retain the catalogue rival.
design.scope: Proposal only: existing target ownership, no new access; no word mapping or test has been supplied.
